subject.title: ACP: support non-thread persistent affinity for cron and orchestrator sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a distinct ACP persistent-affinity contract for cron/hook/orchestrator callers, and what owner/security scope should it enforce?
rationale: Current main intentionally keeps ACP `mode="session"` thread-bound, while this request adds a new non-thread persistent session reuse boundary with security-sensitive ownership semantics.

options.title: Design narrow affinity mode
options.body: Approve a scoped ACP affinity contract limited to cron/hook/orchestrator requesters, with explicit owner identity, backend, cwd, affinity key, lifecycle cleanup, and security tests.

options.title: Track broader decoupled sessions
options.body: Fold this into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53548 and accept a larger product/API design surface.

options.title: Reject core affinity
options.body: Keep ACP persistence only thread-bound in core until a maintainer sponsors the security model for headless reuse.

recommendation.title: Design narrow affinity mode
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped ACP affinity contract limited to cron/hook/orchestrator requesters, with explicit owner identity, backend, cwd, affinity key, lifecycle cleanup, and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows work across requester attribution, docs, and product/security-sensitive ACP surfaces.
